summary: Well-executed, preregistered confirmatory study of template-based input sanitization + deterministic verifier-gating (with limited automated repair) on synthetic adversarial NetOps intents. Artifacts and analysis are archived; primary paired McNemar test (n=141 pairs, n10=6, n01=0) yields a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted configurations (≈0.0426, p=0.03125, 95% bootstrap CI excludes zero). Study limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator, unexecuted benign-control) are acknowledged.
critical_issues: Mandatory Disclosure Statement currently contains execution-level artifacts (several SHA‑256 values and detailed accounting) and reads partially like an execution log; per track rules the Disclosure must be concise and must not duplicate run-internal log detail in prose.

Manuscript must explicitly and prominently state in Methods (and, concisely, at the end of Introduction) that the study used shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore paired-condition differences arise solely from post-generation sanitization/repair and validator gating rather than differing first-pass sampled generations. The current manuscript discusses this, but the explicit statement must appear in the Methods subsection that defines the estimand so readers cannot misread the paired comparison.

The preregistered benign-control and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed. Although the omission is reported, the manuscript must place this fact more prominently in Methods and Results (not only in Limitations/Disclosure) and must remove or rephrase any language that could be read as implying results about benign-input blocking or attack-success beyond the archived formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment).
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise summary that reports the required items (models, orchestration, master-prompt reference, preregistration reference, statement of autonomy boundary, and note that full run artifacts and hashes are archived). Remove non-required execution-log detail and per-file hashes from the in-manuscript Disclosure prose (those remain acceptable in the archived evidence bundle).

Add an explicit, unambiguous sentence in Methods (and repeat as a short clause at the end of the Introduction) stating: 'We used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics; the same initial sampled candidate was reused for paired Baseline and Guarded conditions, so any paired differences derive from post-generation sanitization, verifier-gating, or the permitted repair stage rather than from differing first-pass model samples.'

Prominently report the unexecuted preregistered benign-control (M=50) and false-positive-blocking analysis in Methods and Results (not only in Disclosure/Limitations). Remove any phrasing that could be interpreted as claiming reduced false-positive blocking or improved attacker-success without the executed analyses; keep all claims strictly bounded to the archived formal estimand (validator acceptance).
optional_revisions: Briefly expand the Results paragraph that describes the six discordant (n10) cases with a short, concrete example (archived trace reference and path/hash) to illustrate the repair/sanitization mechanism that enabled acceptance (no new experiments required).

Add a short discussion sentence about practical significance given the high baseline acceptance rate (ceiling effect) and the small absolute effect size, explicitly advising cautious operational interpretation.

Ensure all in-text citations use IEEE bracketed numbering and verify that reference numbers in the bibliography map to the archived verified records (this appears satisfied in the evidence bundle; include one-line verification in the revision log).
